entry.title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
entry.summary: Bérczi, Gehér, Imolay, Lovász, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,α}$, $0<α<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.

entry.title: Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples
entry.summary: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The results do not resolve the unrestricted clique-target problem.
entry.arxiv:comment: 64 pages, main article and technical companion combined; includes computational provenance and verifier source

entry.title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
entry.summary: It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions. We disprove this conjecture by showing that $x_1x_2(x_3x_4+x_5x_6+x_7x_8)$ is not a sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^8$. We extend this construction to obtain counterexamples in every even dimension $n\ge 8$. Using Shaporenko's reduction, we also obtain explicit counterexamples to Tokareva's derivative conjecture in every even dimension $n\ge 10$.
entry.arxiv:comment: The counterexamples and proofs in this paper were obtained through large-scale automated reasoning with LLM agents while solving Problem~10 in NSUCRYPTO~2026 (MiniMax M3.1-Flash-Preview, 19 rounds of up to 100 independent agents between 12 and 18 October 2026, 1889 reports in all), paired with 8 rounds of independent audits (227 reports)

entry.title: A counterexample to Gale's conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$
entry.summary: It is known that for every partition of the sphere $S^2$ of unit diameter into four parts, the largest diameter of a part is at least $\sqrt{(3+\sqrt{3})/6} = 0.88807\dots$, and this bound is attained. The conjecture of D.~Gale (1953) asserts that no set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a larger ratio. In this paper, we construct a $101$-point set $V\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every partition of $V$ into four parts contains a part of diameter greater than $0.88928 \, \operatorname{diam} V$.

entry.title: On minimum-size matroid counterexamples to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality
entry.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $\Tutte_M(x,y)$ be its Tutte polynomial. The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality \[ \Tutte_M(2,0)\Tutte_M(0,2)\geq \Tutte_M(1,1)^2 \] was proved to be false for matroids by Beke, Csáji, Csikvári, and Pituk (\emph{Adv. Math.} \textbf{446} (2024), 109674). Let $U_{n,r}$ denote the rank-$r$ uniform matroid on $n$ elements, where $0<r<n$, and let $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ denote the matroid obtained by replacing each element of $U_{n,r}$ with $q$ parallel copies. They constructed an infinite family of counterexamples of the form $U_{n,r}^{(2)}$, including $U_{33,22}^{(2)}$. In this paper, we prove that every $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ with $q\geq3$ satisfies the inequality. For $q=2$, we prove that the minimum number of elements in such a counterexample is $62$, attained by $U_{31,21}^{(2)}$. For loopless and bridgeless graphs, Noble and Royle (\emph{Eur. J. Comb.} \textbf{38} (2014), 24--35) showed that every edge of a minimum-size counterexample to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh conjecture lies in a series or parallel class of size two or three. For matroids, we further prove that every element of a minimum-size loopless and coloopless counterexample lies in exactly one series or parallel class of size two.

entry.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture and improved bounds for bipanchromatic colorings
entry.summary: We study the bipanchromatic number $χ_B$, introduced by Lalou et al. (Discrete Appl. Math. 391 (2026), 511-522) as the maximum number of colors in a panchromatic hypergraph coloring where every color appears at least twice. They show that merging uniquely occurring colors in a maximum panchromatic coloring gives the lower bound $β=χ_P-\lceilα/2\rceil \leq χ_B$, where $χ_P$ is the panchromatic number and $α$ is the minimum number of such colors among maximum panchromatic colorings. They conjectured that $χ_B=β$ and subsequently disproved it (arXiv:2610.08042). We identify the smallest counterexample, with six vertices and three hyperedges, both minimum possible. We show that the ratio bound $χ_B/β<2$ is asymptotically sharp and prove minimality results for the order and hyperedge count. For $3\leα<χ_P$ we show that every integer from $β$ to $χ_P-1$ occurs as $χ_B$ while $χ_P$ and $α$ are held fixed. Furthermore, we discover that the values $|V|,χ_P,α$ directly decide whether the conjectured equality holds except when $α=4$, where a matching reduction resolves the ambiguity. We derive the optimal universal lower bound $L$ depending only on $|V|,χ_P,α$ in the nontrivial regime $0<2α<|V|$. Finally, we prove $χ_B/L\le5/4$ and $χ_B/L\le6/5+1/(5L)$, with $5/4$ sharp and $6/5$ asymptotically sharp as $L\to\infty$.

entry.title: Counterexamples to Two Conjectures on Tangles in Matroid Minors
entry.summary: We give counterexamples to two conjectures of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle concerning tangles in matroid minors. We construct a matroid $P_0$ with a tangle $\mathcal T$ of order seven. For each $i\in\{4,5,6,7\}$, let $\mathcal T_i$ denote its order-$i$ truncation. No proper minor $N$ of $P_0$ admits, for every such $i$, a tangle of order $i$ whose breadth equals that of $\mathcal T_i$, and $P_0$ is not weakly $4$-connected. We also construct a matroid $P_1$ with a tangle of order four and breadth six, but no internally $4$-connected minor of $P_1$ admits a tangle of order four.

entry.title: Counterexamples to the local antimagic leaf conjecture
entry.summary: It has been conjectured that $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+2$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three, where $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)$ is the local antimagic chromatic number and $\ell(T)$ denotes the number of leaves. We disprove this bound and show that no absolute constant can replace $2$ in an inequality of this form. Our approach uses degree-based intervals containing all possible induced vertex weights under bijective edge labelings, together with a separation criterion that forces selected internal vertex weights to be distinct. We first construct caterpillars $T_3$ and $T_4$ satisfying $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T_3)=\ell(T_3)+3$ and $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T_4)=\ell(T_4)+4$, respectively. We then construct, for every positive integer $r$, infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic caterpillars with exactly $r$ internal vertices for which every bijective edge labeling is antimagic. Each such caterpillar $T$ satisfies $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)=|V(T)|=\ell(T)+r$. Consequently, $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)-\ell(T)$ is unbounded even within the class of caterpillars, and no absolute constant $C$ can satisfy $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+C$ for every tree $T$.

entry.title: A counterexample to the Erdős--Sós bipartite-link conjecture
entry.summary: Erdős and Sós conjectured that every $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph whose link graphs are all bipartite has at most $(1/4+o(1))\binom n3$ edges. We disprove this conjecture by constructing counterexamples with edge density at least $0.250000356>1/4$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

entry.title: A symmetric counterexample to Strang's conjecture for bivariate $C^1$ cubic splines on triangulations
entry.summary: We exhibit a triangulation of an equilateral triangle for which the space of bivariate $C^1$ cubic splines has dimension larger than the dimension formula conjectured by Strang. Notably, the triangulation is such that no two edges sharing a vertex are collinear, and the triangulation is invariant under the action of the isometry group ($D_3$) of the equilateral triangle which is triangulated.

entry.title: A counterexample to the circuit-cocircuit intersection conjecture
entry.summary: Oxley conjectured that a matroid with a circuit-cocircuit intersection of size $k\geq 4$ has one of size $k-2$. Using the standard polynomial representation of the classical extended binary Golay code, we construct an identically self-dual binary matroid of rank $12$ on $24$ elements. Its circuit-cocircuit intersection sizes are exactly $0,2,4,6,8$, and $12$, disproving the conjecture for $k=12$. The proof is self-contained and does not rely on the full weight distribution of the code or on an enumeration of all circuits.

entry.title: Counterexamples to the Strong Roberson Conjecture
entry.summary: We refute the Strong Roberson Conjecture, which asserts that adding any graph outside a class closed under minors and disjoint unions strictly increases the distinguishing power of homomorphism counts from that class. More precisely, we construct connected graphs $H$ for which counts from graphs excluding $H$ as a minor determine the number of homomorphisms from $H$ to any target graph. We also refute the analogous conjecture with immersions in place of minors. We give explicit infinite families of excluded graphs, including cubic bipartite graphs that yield counterexamples for both relations. The proof introduces a method for deriving exact homomorphism count dependence from modular equivalences. We obtain these equivalences for infinitely many primes using prime-order automorphisms of graphs that exclude their orbit quotients as minors or immersions.

entry.title: Non-freezing of the proximity digraph and non-pseudostable convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann--Krause models: Counterexamples to conjectures and results of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo
entry.summary: In 2012, Mirtabatabaei and Bullo studied heterogeneous Hegselmann--Krause models of opinion dynamics, where different agents may have different confidence or influence bounds. They conjectured that opinion vectors always converge, a fundamental problem that remains open. In support of this main conjecture they gave some partial results and made some auxiliary conjectures. Here we give counterexamples to two of these auxiliary conjectures, and even to one theorem in their paper. We explain why these disproved conjectures and false theorem nevertheless likely remain valid for almost all initial opinion vectors. In the last section (Section 7), we describe the role of AI in the production of the results in this paper.
entry.arxiv:comment: Version 2. In V.1, the conditions under which Thm 6.4(iii)(a) of [4] can be rescued were not described accurately. Minor editions to Abstract, Sections 1 and 6. Since V.1 appeared, our results have notably been built on. entry.title: Intersecting integer partitions: star bounds and counterexamples at every scale
entry.summary: Two integer partitions $t$-intersect if they have at least $t$ common parts, counted with multiplicity. We study the largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ positive parts. The canonical $t$-star consists of the partitions containing at least $t$ ones. Applying Kupavskii's weak-spread theorem, we prove that this star is largest whenever $n\ge Ak^3$, for every fixed $A>24$ and all sufficiently large $k$, uniformly over $1\le t<k$. We also give counterexamples to Borg's conjecture at every intersection scale: for all sufficiently large $k$ and for every $1\le t\le \lceil k/4\rceil$, we describe $t$-intersecting families on integer partitions of $n=\lfloor tk^2/3\rfloor$ into $k$ parts which are strictly larger than the corresponding canonical stars. Moreover we present a family of counterexamples to Borg's conjectures about largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ without restricting the number of parts.
entry.arxiv:comment: We added counterexamples to Borg's conjectures about largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions without restricting the number of parts. Additional small edits

entry.title: Morley Simplices in Higher Dimensions: Regularity, Reflections, and Counterexamples
entry.summary: Trisecting the dihedral angles of an $n$-simplex defines its Morley simplex. We study the original simplices for which this simplex is regular. A criterion in terms of the Gram matrix of the facet normals reduces the problem to a matrix equation. The derivative of the Morley map at the regular simplex has two explicit eigenvalues, both nonzero for $n\ge3$; thus the regular simplex is an isolated solution. We conjecture that in dimensions four and five a regular Morley simplex forces two hyperplane reflections interchanging disjoint pairs of vertices. We prove that this conclusion fails in every dimension $6\le n\le200$ and in every dimension $n=\binom k2-1$ with $k\ge9$: in these dimensions there are simplices with regular Morley simplex and no hyperplane reflection symmetry. The examples for $8\le n\le200$ have dihedral symmetry of order $2(n+1)$, while the infinite family is based on the Johnson scheme. In dimension four we give exact constructions of two nonregular examples, defined by irreducible polynomials of degrees $18$ and $8$ with Galois groups $S_{18}$ and $S_8$. Neither example is expressible by radicals. The computer assisted existence proofs use exact rational arithmetic and intervals with outward rounding.

entry.title: Counterexamples to Aigner's majorization conjecture for star-forest search
entry.summary: In adaptive quantitative group testing with exactly two defective items, each test reports how many defectives lie in a chosen subset. We study configurations in which the possible defective pairs form the edges of a star forest. Aigner proved a necessary majorization condition on the ordered star sizes for identifying the defective pair within a prescribed number of tests, and conjectured that this condition was sufficient. We disprove the conjecture by an explicit six-test counterexample and give an analytic family of counterexamples for every test budget $k\ge6$. The obstruction uses two tight prefix sums to force incompatible demands on the outcomes of the first test. We also prove, by exhaustive computation combined with analytic reductions, that the converse holds for $0\le k\le5$. Thus six is the first test budget at which majorization alone fails. The counterexamples and their infinite extension do not depend on the exhaustive computation.
